appearance.organs.note: How the grass program's organs are drawn, shared by every built-in grass (visual forms Skill 1, 2026-10-14): a leaf as pieces of an untapered blade card that ends in a tapered tip piece, dead leaves likewise, and the flowering head as a cluster of spikelets, as the family's inflorescence_unit states. The rules fill in the cluster and the spikelet from the characters.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the grass base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the grass program gave as defaults until then.
The program the authors chose to grow this taxon's shrub species (named in each species' spec until G2.3a moved it here).

rules.appearance.organs.panicle.colour.note: How PlantGen colours an organ from the colour a source states for the species, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 3, 2026-10-14): the stated colour itself, on the looks' 0 to 1 scale.

traits.inflorescence_unit.note: VicFlora's family description: the flowers sit in spikelets, two rows of bracts on a small axis, the lowest two (glumes) empty and each one above (a lemma) holding a small flower with its palea.

traits.scale_arrangement.note: VicFlora's family description: a spikelet's bracts stand in two rows on its small axis, the glumes at the foot and a lemma above each, so each bract is on the other side from the one below.

traits.leaf_form.note: Families of Flowering Plants of Australia: a grass leaf is a sheath round the stem and a blade above it, with a small flap or ring of hairs where they meet.

traits.leaf_division.note: Families of Flowering Plants of Australia: the blade is one undivided strip.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Families of Flowering Plants of Australia: blades usually linear.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Families of Flowering Plants of Australia: the veins run side by side along the blade.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Families of Flowering Plants of Australia: one leaf at each node, alternating.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Families of Flowering Plants of Australia: the leaves stand in two ranks, each node turned half a turn from the last.

traits.fruit_type.note: Families of Flowering Plants of Australia: the fruit is a caryopsis (a grain).

rules.note: How PlantGen's grass program draws a grass from a flora's sizes, a choice of the model's until grasses are built from their spikelets (spec rework M6): its mean blade length is the blade length a flora gives, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical length, and its panicle the inflorescence's length. The program builds a blade from `pieces` pieces, each 12% shorter than the one before, so the first is 0.12 / (1 - 0.88^pieces) of the blade; the blade card narrows 12% along a piece, so one width over length serves every piece and the tip.

traits.woodiness.note: Hitchcock's family description (p. 15-16): grasses are herbs, rarely woody plants; the bamboos' culms and those of a few other genera are woody.

traits.flowering_position.note: Hitchcock's family description (p. 15): the spikelets are nearly always gathered into spikes or panicles at the ends of the main culms or of branches.

traits.inflorescence.note: Hitchcock's account of the grass inflorescence (p. 8-9): the panicle is the commonest kind of grass cluster, the spike (sessile spikelets) is the Hordeae's and Chlorideae's, and a true raceme is rare in grasses.

traits.glumes.note: Hitchcock's family description (p. 15) and account of the glumes (p. 9): the lowest two bracts of a spikelet are the empty glumes; rarely one or both are obsolete (first glume wanting in Paspalum, Digitaria; both in Leersia).

traits.sexual_system.note: Hitchcock's family description (p. 15): flowers perfect, rarely unisexual; his keys name a few monoecious genera (maize's tribe, Tripsaceae, p. 16-17) and dioecious ones (e.g. Buchloe, Distichlis).

traits.leaf_margin.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA), Gramineae: the blades' margins nearly always entire.

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 262, 264, family Poaceae: life span perennial or annual; read as {"annual": "often", "perennial": "often"}.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 262, 264, family Poaceae: rhizome habit long_creeping (rhizomes or stolons in perennials), often; read as {"long_creeping": "often"}.

traits.clonal.note: Ingrouille, Diversity and Evolution of Land Plants (1992) p. 267, 268, family Poaceae: clonal true, usually; read as {"true": "usually"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Gramineae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome, rarely tubers. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

appearance.organs.panicle.colour.why: A grass's panicle is drawn in the colour its spikelets, its showiest part in flower, are stated in.

generator.params.leaf_length.why: A grass's blades are as long on average as floras measure them.

generator.params.panicle_length.why: A grass's panicle is as long as floras measure its inflorescence.

appearance.organs.blade.shape.aspect.why: A blade card is a piece of a blade, the first piece as wide as the blade at its widest: its width over the first piece's length.

appearance.organs.blade_tip.shape.aspect.why: The tip of a blade narrows as the pieces below it do, so its card has their width over length.

appearance.organs.thatch.shape.aspect.why: Thatch is last year's blades, as wide as they were.
